chapter: The Blakey quartet on the road
title: Bookings by Willard Alexander and Billy Shaw, and road manager Milt Gray
summary: He tells how the quartet was booked and how Gray took ham and plates from restaurants.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We played all over; we played a lot of clubs, different cities. We played Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Washington—where else did we play—we played St. Louis, California a lot. I can’t remember the names of the clubs; especially in L.A. we played quite a few clubs in L.A. We did good business.
Did you have a manager booking you?

Yeah, Willard Alexander booked my group, basically. I did have Billy Shaw for a while book my group, and I had a road manage that was also another story; his name was Milt Gray and he was from Philadelphia. And he was, I could never call him a thief, he wasn’t a thief, but sometimes when we played New York he’d come up with different items from motel lobbies and hotel lobbies and…
Souvenirs, yeah. One time he had an apartment and somehow managed to furnish this place with different pieces from around the city. He, Frank DeVito was a…

…and Milt Gray picking up pieces of ham and bacon in his coat walking, sometimes he’d pick up, in a restaurant, he’d pick up plates and he had this coat he’d put in these pocket and be walking with these plates and stuff.
No, it was just, he [laughter], I don’t know. Frank said to him, “Why did you pick up that ham?” He says, “Because I like ham with my breakfast.” [laughter]
